About this role
Your Team
Internal Audit’s primary mission is to provide assurance to the Board of Directors and Executive Management that BlackRock’s businesses are well managed and meeting strategic, operational and risk management objectives. The team engages with senior leaders and all of BlackRock’s individual business units globally to understand and advise on the risks in their business, evaluate the effectiveness of key processes and assist in the design of best practices that can improve their results. Internal Audit reports directly to the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors, and our work builds confidence that BlackRock will meet its obligations to clients, shareholders, employees and other stakeholders.
The Business Audit team operates across the US, Europe, and Asia, and conducts audits covering all BlackRock business units, including investment management, risk management, operations, finance, legal and compliance, and client businesses.
Your Role and Impact
As a Business Audit Associate, you will contribute to the execution of regional and global audit engagements, helping to assess risks, evaluate key business processes, and support a strong control environment across BlackRock. You will work closely with stakeholders across a variety of business functions, gaining broad exposure to the asset management industry while developing expertise in risk assessment, audit methodology, and business process evaluation. Your work will help drive meaningful insights, support effective risk management, and contribute to the continued strength and resilience of the organization
Your Responsibilities
In every role at BlackRock, you'll be expected to apply sound judgement and critical thinking to solve complex problems, adapt as the business evolves, and combine the curiosity to explore new approaches and technologies with the rigor to challenge the results. The scope of this role also includes the following responsibilities:
• Perform regional and global audit reviews, engaging with stakeholders to understand and document key processes and risks and prepare clear process narratives and briefing materials.
• Evaluate the design and operation of key processes, investigate and escalate issues identified through testing, and validate the effective remediation of findings.
• Identify emerging firm-wide and business risks and understanding key changes in strategies and operating mode through ongoing engagements with business management.
• Contribute to global departmental initiatives.
• Travel to regional and international locations may be required.
Your Experience
• Undergraduate or graduate degree and 3+ years of relevant experience, preferably in financial services or internal audit, with an understanding of financial instruments and asset management processes and risks.
• Interest in broad exposure to investment management, sales, trading, operations, risk management, finance, and compliance, and relevant regulatory and industry developments.
• Relevant professional qualifications or certifications, such as Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA), Chartered Accountant (CA), Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), Investment Management Certificate (IMC), or another relevant professional qualification, is a plus.
• Strong verbal, written, listening, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to build effective working relationships with peers and business partners.
• Intellectual curiosity, professional skepticism, and strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to communicate complex subjects clearly and concisely.
• Strong project management, organizational, and data analysis capabilities.
• Practitioner-level AI fluency with demonstrated judgement.
Our benefits
To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of employee benefits including: retirement investment and tools designed to help you in building a sound financial future; access to education reimbursement; comprehensive resources to support your physical health and emotional well-being; family support programs; and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about.
Our hybrid work model
BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock.
Guidance on AI use for candidates
At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self.
About BlackRock
At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being.  Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress.
This mission would not be possible without our smartest investment – the one we make in our employees. It’s why we’re dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues feel welcomed, valued and supported with networks, benefits and development opportunities to help them thrive.
To learn more about BlackRock, please visit Careers.BlackRock.com. We also encourage you to get to know us on LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, X, and TikTok.
BlackRock is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.  We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to age, disability, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation and other protected characteristics at law.

•    Ensure there is sufficient ink supply for up to 24 hours.  As the production plan is subject to change, ensure the 24 hour threshold is not breached.
•    Make full use of the eXact spectro, IFS6 and IQC, to reduce press downtime to a minimum.
•    Log press returns back into the system for future ease of use.
•    Assist the Printers on press should any minor adjustments be required, making any changes to the system recipe as required.
•    Maintain the distillation plant and optimise waste inks and solvent, ensuring waste generated is minimised as much as possible.
•    Assist the Ink Room Manager with other duties as and when required.  Specifically, help with the offloading of ink deliveries and support stock takes and re-ordering of ink supplies.

When joining PerkinElmer, you select an experienced and trusted leader in scientific solutions, with the support of a global service network and distribution centers, providing the right solution, at the right time, to meet critical customer needs.  With over an 80+ year legacy of advancing science and a mission of innovating for a healthier world, our dedicated team collaborates closely with commercial, government, academic and healthcare customers to deliver our broad portfolio of analytical solutions, and OneSource services.
Job Title
Senior Electronics Design Engineer, Laboratory Instruments
Location(s)
High Wycombe
Job Description
About the role
Hands-on senior designer in a mission-driven electronics team developing the next generation of material-characterisation laboratory instruments and sustaining the existing product range. You will own subsystems from requirements to verified hardware: low-noise detection front-ends, power distribution, MCU- and FPGA-based control boards, and the integration of cables, actuators and motors. You bring the two things the team needs most: a structured product-design approach and high-speed digital / Xilinx FPGA capability.
What you will do
• Design and verify circuits for the new instrument: low-noise analogue front-ends, mixed-signal, power and control boards.
• Own high-speed digital and FPGA/SoC (Xilinx Zynq) design, and PCB design in Altium 365 to IPC standards.
• Take technical ownership of the electronics architecture for your subsystems, from early concept through prototype, verification and product release.
• Run the product-design process for your subsystems: hardware and product requirements (HRS/PRS), design proposals, design reviews, DFMEA, verification plans and reports.
• Prototype quickly — breadboards, proto and rework boards — to validate concepts ahead of full PCBA spins.
• Bring up, debug and validate boards on the bench with the firmware team; solder, modify and test hardware yourself.
• Own the electrical BOM, component datasheets and the related safety/EMC considerations; support DFM/DFA as designs move from prototype to production.
• Sustain released products: obsolescence and alternates, manufacturing and field issues, root cause.
• Work with optics, mechanics, firmware, software and scientists to prove out designs; coordinate cross-functional issue resolution.
Essential
• Degree in electrical/electronic engineering or a closely related discipline; 5+ years of design engineering in instrumentation or test & measurement products.
• Mixed-signal design in a low-noise environments.
• Digital hardware: MCU-based control boards and communication interfaces — 1G/10GEthernet, USB, SPI, I²C, UART/RS-232, RS-485, CAN, PCIe.
• High-speed multilayer (8+ layer) digital design from schematic to PCB, including DDR3/DDR4 memory interfaces; FPGA/SoC design on Xilinx Zynq in VHDL or Verilog.
• Schematic and PCB design in Altium 365 to IPC-2221 / IPC-7351 with managed-library and version-control discipline; design for manufacture and assembly with a contract manufacturer, including DFM checks (e.g. Valor NPI) and Gerber review (e.g. ViewMate).
• Hands-on PCBA bring-up, test and troubleshooting with digital oscilloscopes, DVMs, spectrum, and logic analysers; test rigs and test plans; disciplined root-cause analysis. Not afraid of practical work — tinkering with circuits and debugging on your own initiative.
• EMC and product safety for laboratory equipment: IEC 61326-1 and IEC 61010-1, through to passing compliance testing.
• Structured product-design approach: requirements, design reviews, DFMEA, verification plans and reports.
• Obsolescence management and sustaining of released products.
• System-integration mindset: how a board fits the rest of the system — cabling, connectivity, harnessing, system diagrams — not only what it does.
Desirable
• Experience with power supply design.
• Working with suppliers and manufacturers: quotes, cost comparisons, assembly options.
• Familiarity with PLM and task-tracking tools.
• Git and Git-based workflows; lean product development with Jira and Confluence.
• Applied use of AI tools and agentic workflows in engineering work
• UV instruments and high-voltage lamp drivers; thermal control and thermal-equipment design.
How we work
• Analytical and data-driven, with attention to detail; sees both the small and the big picture.
• Task- and goal-oriented and well organised; works independently or as part of a larger team; comfortable in a high-paced, hands-on hardware environment.
• Communicates clearly in writing and in person; adaptable across several projects with shifting priorities and deadlines.
• Open-minded and confident to push back on design changes and tasks when the evidence says so.
• A problem-solver and fixer: not afraid to break things, cut to the cause and debug quickly.
• Brings energy, mentors others and helps grow the team.
What we offer
• A well-equipped personal bench, all the test equipment and software you need.
• A lab and instrument set-up that is being built now — you will help shape it.
• Cross-discipline project teams; an electronics team of two engineers plus placement students; direct influence on the next-generation instruments.

Location: Immingham

We're looking for a Machine Preparation Centre (MPC) Engineer to join our team in Immingham. In this hands-on role, you'll be responsible for preparing, inspecting, and commissioning new Volvo Construction Equipment machines to the highest standards of safety, quality, and customer satisfaction. Working as part of the Machine Preparation Centre team, you'll ensure every machine is fully prepared, configured, and ready for delivery, while supporting continuous improvement and maintaining SMT GB's commitment to engineering excellence.

• Carrying out pre-delivery inspections (PDI), machine preparation, commissioning activities, and fitting customer-specified attachments and accessories.
• Completing all inspections, software updates, documentation, and PDA inputs accurately, ensuring machines meet OEM and customer requirements before release.
• Identifying and reporting defects, additional work requirements, or technical concerns to ensure issues are resolved efficiently.
• Maintaining company tools, equipment, and work areas to high standards while complying with all Health & Safety, COSHH, quality, and environmental procedures.
• Supporting colleagues, mentoring trainees where required, attending technical training courses, and contributing to the overall success of the Preparation Centre.
What You'll Need
We're looking for a motivated and detail-focused engineer with experience in the repair, maintenance, or preparation of heavy construction plant, agricultural machinery, HGVs, or similar equipment. You'll have a strong understanding of hydraulic and electrical systems, a commitment to quality workmanship, and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment.
• A recognised engineering qualification in Plant Maintenance, Agricultural Engineering, HGV Mechanics, or a related discipline (e.g. NVQ Level 2, City & Guilds or equivalent).
• Experience preparing, servicing, or repairing heavy plant equipment, with good diagnostic and problem-solving skills across hydraulic and electrical systems.
• Strong communication, organisational, and teamwork skills, with a proactive approach and excellent attention to detail.
• Basic IT skills, including the ability to use email, digital systems, and technical documentation, alongside a continuous improvement mindset.
• A full UK driving licence is desirable, while welding experience would be advantageous. Flexibility to attend training courses, work occasional overtime, and stay away from home when required is also essential.
What's in it for You?
Alongside a competitive salary, we offer a great range of benefits to support your health, wellbeing, finances, and life outside of work, including:
• Health & Wellbeing: Health Cash Plan, 24/7 GP service, free physiotherapy access, and a wide range of wellbeing support.
• Family & Lifestyle Support: Enhanced sick pay, maternity, paternity and adoption leave, IVF support, and retirement benefits.
• Financial Benefits: Pension with up to 5% matched contributions, Cycle to Work scheme, EV salary sacrifice schemes, and employee discounts.
• Recognition & Community: Refer-a-friend bonuses, long service awards, volunteering days, and recognition through our Caring, Daring, Sharing awards programme.
• Additional Perks: Christmas shutdown as part of your annual leave entitlement, plus opportunities to get involved through our Employee Council and Social Committee.
Closing date & interview process
We review applications on an ongoing basis and may close this advert early if sufficient suitable applications are received. Early application is therefore encouraged.

Our way of working as a professional community, can be best described as Caring, Daring and Sharing. Caring because we are service-minded, and we always like to go the extra mile for our customers and give our people the attention and care they deserve. Daring because we are innovative in our business, constantly looking for smart improvement. nvidia.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/nvidiaexter.description_excerpt:
NVIDIA is looking for a Senior Network and Fabric Operations Solutions Architect to join its NVIDIA Infrastructure Specialist Team. Academic and commercial organizations around the world are using NVIDIA products to redefine deep learning and data analytics, and to power next-generation data centres. Join the team building and advising on the networks behind many of the largest and fastest AI/HPC systems in the world!
We are looking for someone who combines deep networking expertise with strong consulting and communication skills. This role will engage directly with customers, partners and cross-functional teams to assess, architect and operate the compute, storage and scale-up fabrics that underpin large GPU estates—serving as both a trusted advisor and a hands-on technical leader. You will own the fabric side of NVIDIA’s Cloud Partner (NCP) operating model across the full Day 1 to Day 2 lifecycle: from InfiniBand/UFM and Ethernet validation at handover, through NVLink partition operations, to a production-stable fabric running at maximum goodput. NCP estates are open-source-first and heterogeneous—Cumulus Linux, SONiC, Spectrum-X, DOCA/DPU services, upstream Kubernetes and Prometheus/Grafana—so this role is deliberately tool-agnostic: you will meet each partner on the fabric they actually run rather than on a single proprietary product.
What You’ll Be Doing:
•
Own Day 2 fabric operations across NCP fleets: NVLink/NVSwitch partition management (NMX-C / NMX-M) on GB200/GB300 NVL72-class systems, maintenance-partition isolation, and safe partition-change workflows for multi-tenant estates.
•
Own the switch software and firmware lifecycle—Cumulus Linux, SONiC and switch-OS upgrades, CPLD and field-notice rollout campaigns—with staged, tested upgrade plans that keep partner fabrics off stale releases without disrupting production workloads.
•
Support Day 1 fabric validation and acceptance: InfiniBand and UFM bring-up, Spectrum-X/RoCE Ethernet configuration, cabling and link-health verification, routing and congestion-control validation, and multi-day, multi-rack burn-in against agreed MTBI and goodput targets.
•
Minimise the time from cluster handover to first production workload, removing duplicated fabric validation across hardware bring-up, managed-service intake and the partner’s own network operations teams.
•
Drive fabric reliability at fleet scale: telemetry for link flaps, retransmits and congestion, fault detection through to remediation, root-cause analysis of network-induced job failures, and measurable improvement of MTBI and job goodput.
•
Provide consultative guidance and hands-on troubleshooting across the fabric stack—NICs and DPUs, switch OS, routing and congestion control, host networking and Kubernetes network integration—and act as the technical leader for assigned accounts, running structured knowledge transfer and producing runbooks so partner teams can operate advanced fabric configurations independently.
What We Need to See:
•
BS/MS/PhD in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or related fields, or equivalent experience.
•
5+ years of professional experience in data centre networking, fabric engineering or large-scale network operations roles.
•
Fabric & Data Centre Networking: Deep understanding of data centre network architectures and RDMA fabrics—InfiniBand and RoCE/Ethernet—including topology and routing design (fat-tree, rail-optimised), congestion control, lossless/QoS configuration, and troubleshooting across NICs, switches and high-speed interconnects.
•
NVIDIA Fabric Technologies: Hands-on experience with InfiniBand and UFM, Spectrum-X Ethernet, Cumulus Linux and/or SONiC, ConnectX and BlueField NICs/DPUs, and NVLink/NVSwitch systems—ideally including NMX-C / NMX-M partition operations on NVL72-class platforms.
•
Linux & Switch Platforms: Deep knowledge of Linux (RedHat, Ubuntu) and switch operating systems, network OS internals, host networking and OS-level security, together with an understanding of the storage and compute traffic patterns of HPC/AI clusters.
•
Automation, GitOps & Observability: Proficiency in Python and Bash scripting, configuration management and Infrastructure-as-Code tools (e.g. Ansible, Terraform), GitOps-based network configuration and firmware/upgrade management for large fleets, and observability stacks (Grafana, Loki, Prometheus) applied to fabric telemetry.
•
Fleet Reliability & Customer Engagement: Demonstrated ability to measure and improve MTBI and job goodput on large GPU clusters—fault detection, drain and remediation workflows, SLO/error-budget definition and post-incident review—combined with a strong consultative background leading architectural reviews and presenting to executive stakeholders.
Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:
•
Experience operating Kubernetes networking in GPU clusters—CNI plugins, multi-network attachment, SR-IOV and RDMA device plugins—and with the NVIDIA Network and GPU Operators for automated resource lifecycle management.
•
Expertise with DOCA and DPU infrastructure services (e.g. DOCA DPF) for offloaded networking, security and storage services.
•
Familiarity with fabric and GPU health telemetry—DCGM and XID diagnostics, link-level and switch counters, node-level health agents, and fleet-wide reliability intelligence.
•
Knowledge of large-scale training traffic behaviour: collective communication (NCCL) tuning, rail alignment, and diagnosing network-bound performance regressions in distributed training jobs.
•
Experience delivering multi-tenant network isolation for GPU-as-a-service estates—VRF/VLAN/EVPN segmentation, tenant partitioning and secure fabric handover between tenants.

Mentor and technically supervise Senior and Intermediate Structural Engineers within the team

Job Description:
Mechanical Engineering Graduate Apprentice
Your impact
At Leonardo we have an opportunity for school/college leavers or individuals already in work and looking for a new career path, to join the Radar and Advanced Targeting line of business as a Mechanical Engineering Graduate Apprentice working in our design team. Your role as a Leonardo Mechanical Engineering Graduate Apprentice will be to support the design and development of our world leading radar and electro-optic products under the guidance of experienced Mechanical Engineers. Our new Graduate Apprentice scheme will enable you to learn how to use state-of-the-art methods, technology and tools to explore all aspects of the product lifecycle, including stress and thermal analysis, requirements analysis, design, implementation, test, build and product support.
Role description
Leonardo’s Mechanical Engineering Graduate Apprenticeship is a 4-year scheme based in Edinburgh. We are looking for people who have a strong interest in technical / STEM related activities, who understand the importance of communication, and who are able to work well as part of a team and also using their own initiative. You will have the drive and commitment to work through difficult problems to find the right engineering solutions. Throughout the duration of your apprenticeship, you will have the opportunity to rotate through different projects and phases of the product lifecycle in order to accelerate your competency development.
Your working week will consist of a minimum of 3-days on-the-job training alongside 1-2 days protected study to allow you to complete your academic studies.
You will study at Heriot Watt University in Edinburgh for completion of a BEng (Hons) in Engineering: Design & Manufacture (Mechanical) through a mixture of work-based learning, distance learning and day release at university. During the teaching semesters, you will be required to attend University classes, seminars and labs on campus one day a week. Leonardo also gives up to an additional 1 day per week to work towards your academic studies. Attendance at University classes is mandatory and must be treated in the same way as any other working day.
Upon completion of your Graduate Apprenticeship, you will attain a BSc (Hons) Engineering: Design & Manufacture (Mechanical) degree.

• Contribute directly to the development and delivery of our cutting-edge Radar, Laser and Infra-red countermeasure products as either a member of one of our Integrated Project Teams (IPTs) or as a member of our central analysis team.
• Receive training in both technical and soft skills which are tailored to the particular role and area of the business you are in.
• The opportunity to accelerate competency attainment through rotational placements around different projects or stages of the product lifecycle, to enable you to become a well-rounded engineer.
• Continue professional development throughout your career through formal training, site visits, internal awareness sessions, learning from more experienced engineers and keeping up to date with the latest technical developments, both internal to Leonardo and in wider industry.

4 Higher Grades (or equivalent): BBBB

Preferred:  English and another STEM subject e.g.  Graphic Communication, Product Design, Craft & Design, Tech Studies, Computing, Woodwork, Metalwork etc.
AND
Standard Grades (1-3) / National 5: (A-C) in English
Note: SAAS funding from English apprentices moving to Scotland must have residency in Scotland before 1st August 2027.
The starting salary for this role is £23,500
During your Apprenticeship we encourage you to spend at least 3/4 days a week on site to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience.

At Leonardo, many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.

You will own the analytical models and frameworks that connect product behavior to business outcomes across acquisition, activation, adoption, expansion, and renewal.

• Develop causal and inferential analyses that connect product interactions to revenue outcomes (NRR, LTV, expansion)

• Deep expertise in predictive modelling, causal inference, survival analysis, and experimentation (A/B, diff-in-diff, instrumental variables)
• Experience working directly with product telemetry and event-stream data at scale

About the Job
Every week, Business Talent Group (BTG) matches independent consultants, subject-matter experts, and interim executives to live problems inside some of the world's biggest companies — over half the Fortune 100 come to us when they need senior talent fast. As a Heidrick & Struggles company, we sit at the centre of the on-demand talent economy, and our London-based Client Service team is growing to keep up.
We're hiring a Client Service Lead (4+ years' experience) to own the full talent-delivery process on their own projects, build strong client and talent relationships, and begin coaching the associates around them. This is the step up from independent execution to owning outcomes, advising clients directly, and helping build the next generation of the team.
What You'll Actually Be Doing
Our clients come to us for critical, time-sensitive challenges, and we work at pace to find the right talent solution — from an interim CFO for a PE-backed business to an AI transformation leader for a UK bank. Whatever the brief, you will:
• Drive the search, end to end. Own every step of talent delivery on your own projects, from the first client conversation through to talent offboarding: deciding on search approach, shortlisting the candidates you recommend, and shaping how they're positioned to the client.
• Qualify the right talent. Identify and qualify interim executives and independent consultants from within our network or through external search, asking the right questions and drilling down to really understand their capabilities and cultural fit. That means being comfortable picking up the phone for every conversation, including the challenging ones: delivering difficult feedback, coaching a talent, or negotiating rate.
• Bring talent to life for clients. Present talent on client calls with confidence, acting as the go-to expert and advisor on all things talent, from market availability to fit and rate.
• Lead on contracting. Lead contracting and talent onboarding for your projects in collaboration with our contracts team, following best practice to stay compliant, and lead negotiations with talent, including resolving any issues that come up.
• Build your network and your expertise. Cultivate deep relationships with talent on projects and in your area of focus, specialise in that area over time, stay current on relevant news and trends, and use that knowledge to spot opportunities and improve how BTG finds and delivers talent.
• Coach and support associates. Mentor junior team members and give associates and new hires the chance to shadow your work and learn from it.
• Stay on top of your numbers. Consistently hit your targets without needing reminders, review your own performance, and help review the performance of associates you work with.
• Grow accounts through repeat business. Partner with the sales lead on existing accounts, contributing to growth through repeat engagements and extensions.
• Champion growth and efficiency. Help build the UK Client Service team as we grow lean and fast: take initiative, spot ways to sharpen how we work, and champion new tech and AI tools that improve the quality and speed of our delivery, drawing on best practices from other Heidrick solution areas and our On-Demand Talent colleagues in the US and DACH.

A successful Client Service Lead excels at cultivating talent relationships, naturally positions themself as a subject-matter expert in the interim space, and becomes a trusted advisor to clients. Experienced Leads typically grow into a Director role within Client Service, taking on broader commercial, operational, and people leadership responsibility: managing a larger portfolio of projects and accounts, partnering with sales to build out dedicated, strategic client relationships, deepening into an industry or talent specialism and becoming a go-to voice on it, driving process and best-practice improvements across the wider commercial organisation, and creating and delivering training while coaching both Associates and Leads. As the on-demand talent space keeps growing and evolving, other senior opportunities across the Heidrick organisation may open up along the way.
Life at BTG & Heidrick
You'll be based alongside our Heidrick & Struggles colleagues at 31 St James's Square — one office, one culture, with day-to-day access to a global leadership advisory firm rather than a standalone interim outfit. That means access to group-wide training programmes beyond BTG's own onboarding, and an annual Europe & Africa conference that brings together associates, leads, and engagement managers from across the region to connect, learn, and build a network most people don't have access to until much later in their careers.
What We're Looking For
• 4+ years of work experience within the interim, search, or consulting and recruitment space, or other client-facing professional services environment.
• A strong advisor mindset. You look for opportunities beyond the immediate ask; advising clients and talent, and spotting ways to improve how we work.
• Confident under pressure. You can lead a client conversation, scope a project, and negotiate with talent, often across multiple live projects at once.
• A natural coach. You're ready to mentor associates, create shadowing opportunities, and set an example in how you interact with clients and talent.
• Detail-oriented and compliant. You take contracting, onboarding, and compliance seriously, and hold yourself to a high service standard.
• Genuinely curious about business. You actively build knowledge of your industry or specialism and bring that perspective into your project work.
• Comfortable with change. You thrive in a fast-moving, lean team, take initiative without waiting to be asked, and pivot easily as new tools and technologies transform how the On-Demand Talent business works.
• Strong business writing and professional speaking skills.
• Undergraduate degree with a strong academic record.
• Right to work in the UK.
The Details
• Bonus: Annual performance-based bonus, plus quarterly commission payouts.
• Benefits: Pension, private health and dental cover, life assurance, income protection insurance, 25 days' holiday + Christmas closing.
• Working model: Hybrid — flexible split between our London office and home.

Finance Data Engineer
The practice
Finance is one of the most demanding and valuable environments in which to apply modern technology. You will work with complex enterprise data, mission-critical processes and high-impact decisions, using AI, data and engineering to reshape how organisations plan, control performance and allocate resources. The opportunity goes beyond building technically strong solutions: you will see how those solutions influence cash, profitability, risk and business growth, and take them from experimentation into trusted, production-ready capabilities. Working in Finance Reinvention allows you to remain close to leading-edge technology while developing an understanding of the CFO agenda, gaining exposure to senior decision-makers and building the commercial judgement needed to solve enterprise-wide challenges. This combination of deep technical capability, finance-domain expertise and measurable business impact creates a differentiated career path that is difficult to develop in a purely technology-focused role.
Purpose of the role
Responsible for the finance data and ontology layer on which agentic solutions depend. Builds the entities, relationships, definitions, lineage and data contracts sourced from live ERP and EPM systems to a standard that supports controlled and auditable agent behaviour. The role owns governed finance data products, semantic models and retrieval-ready data services that are secure, permission-aware, observable and suitable for AI, analytics and decision intelligence.
Responsibilities
• Build and extend the finance ontology covering supplier, invoice, customer, receivable, journal, account, cost centre and forecast line, and the relationships between them, including controlled vocabularies, business glossaries, hierarchy history, ownership and lifecycle versioning.
• Engineer pipelines from SAP, Oracle, Workday and EPM platforms into governed data products, supporting structured and unstructured sources, batch and incremental ingestion, APIs, files and change-data-capture patterns as appropriate.
• Build entity-resolution and master or reference-data capabilities that reconcile identifiers, definitions and hierarchies across source systems and preserve source-to-target mappings.
• Establish lineage and evidence sufficient for audit, so that agent output can be traced to source, with automated data-quality checks, finance reconciliations, completeness and freshness measures, observability, alerts and recoverable operations.
• Define data contracts between delivery pods, and between Accenture delivery and client platform teams, including schemas, quality thresholds, access rules, service levels, versioning and change-control expectations.
• Experience deploying software or data products on Azure, AWS or GCP, DataBricks, Snowflake, Palantir etc using relevant cloud services and at least one of containers, Kubernetes or serverless patterns.
• Work with AI Engineers on retrieval and grounding, ensuring models receive appropriately scoped context, including chunking and embedding strategies, hybrid or graph retrieval, permission-aware filtering, provenance and retrieval evaluation.
• Implement security and privacy controls across the data lifecycle, including role- or attribute-based access, row or document-level permissions, masking or tokenisation, retention, tenant isolation and audit logging.
• Apply software and DataOps practices including Git, automated testing, CI/CD, infrastructure as code where relevant, performance tuning, cost optimisation and production support.
• Collaborate with finance SMEs, data owners, architects and governance teams to agree definitions, resolve data issues and embed sustainable stewardship and operating ownership.

• Working knowledge of finance data structures, including chart of accounts, entity hierarchy, sub-ledger to ledger relationships, intercompany and period close, together with actual, budget and forecast data, currencies, consolidation and management hierarchies.
• Strong data modelling discipline and the ability to justify and maintain definitional standards, including canonical or semantic models, data contracts, schema evolution, metadata, lineage and data-quality controls.
• Experience extracting and reconciling data from enterprise applications or complex operational systems using APIs, files, database interfaces or change-data-capture patterns.
• Experience deploying software or data products on Azure, AWS or GCP, DataBricks, Snowflake, Palantir etc. using relevant cloud services and at least one of containers, Kubernetes or serverless patterns. (AI engineer – desirable)
• Understanding of secure data engineering, including access control, encryption, secrets, privacy, retention and the handling of sensitive or regulated data.
• Ability to work with finance SMEs and technical teams to translate business definitions and controls into implementable data products and acceptance criteria.
• At least 10 years’ relevant professional experience
• Knowledge graph, semantic layer or ontology engineering experience, including technologies or standards such as Neo4j, RDF/OWL, SKOS, SPARQL or GraphRAG.
• Data quality, master data management or lineage tooling experience, including entity resolution, business glossaries, catalogues or platforms such as Collibra, Purview or Unity Catalog.
• Exposure to SOX or external audit requirements, GDPR, model-risk controls or regulated-data environments.
• Detailed knowledge of one or more finance-platform data models, such as SAP S/4HANA, Oracle Fusion, Workday Financials, Anaplan, OneStream or SAP Analytics Cloud.

Job Description
Location: London, UK (Hybrid: 3 days in office)

So, who are we?
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.

This role sits within the Product function, reporting into the Head of Product - Lifecycle. Product strategy and roadmap

Discovery and delivery

• Navigate regulatory requirements and translate compliance constraints into seamless customer experiences.
• Work comfortably with APIs, backend infrastructure, and platform integrations.

We're looking for a scientifically driven leader with strong biologics development experience and the ability to influence across complex, matrixed environments.

Desirable

You will work in an increasingly AI-augmented engineering environment. We are looking for people who are curious about AI-augmented engineering and willing to experiment with tools that improve software delivery. You will not be expected to use AI tools every day, but you should be open to applying them where they provide clear value, while validating outputs for correctness, security and maintainability.
Working closely with product managers, designers, engineers, and architects, you will turn product requirements into well-structured, maintainable, production-ready solutions. You will take ownership of significant features and services, contribute to technical decisions, support other engineers and help maintain high standards of engineering quality.

•
Build and maintain reliable JVM-based services using Kotlin or modern Java.
•
Design and develop APIs and integrations following industry standards.
•
Contribute to API design standards and documentation.
•
Deliver complete end-to-end features by connecting backend services and data with responsive web interfaces.
•
Use appropriate test-first and test-informed practices to create effective automated tests.
•
Experiment with AI-assisted engineering tools where they provide clear value, such as exploring solutions, improving tests, documenting systems or investigating issues.
•
Validate AI-assisted outputs for correctness, security, maintainability, and suitability before using them.
•
Contribute to event-driven workflows and asynchronous processing.
•
Participate in technical discovery, spikes, architecture discussions and peer code reviews.
•
Improve build, test and deployment pipelines to support safe and efficient delivery.
•
Embed structured logging, metrics and distributed tracing to make services easier to operate and troubleshoot.
•
Consider the operational, security and governance implications of engineering decisions, particularly in complex or regulated environments.
•
Identify and address technical debt, performance issues and reliability risks.
•
Share knowledge, support collective code ownership and contribute to a collaborative, low-ego team culture.
What's important to us
•
Strong commercial experience developing server-side applications with Kotlin or modern Java, ideally Java 17 or later.
•
Good knowledge of the JVM ecosystem and common backend development practices.
•
Experience designing, building and operating APIs.
•
Understanding of service reliability, maintainability, performance and security.
•
Proven experience writing effective automated tests.
•
Practical experience with relational databases.
•
Experience with modern frontend development, ideally using React and TypeScript.
•
Familiarity with CI/CD practices and supporting software in production.
•
Experience working collaboratively in an agile, product-focused engineering team.
•
Curiosity about AI-augmented engineering and a willingness to develop new ways of working.
•
A thoughtful approach to code quality, technical trade-offs and continuous improvement.
Desirable experience
•
Practical experience using AI-assisted development or productivity tools in a software engineering context.
•
Familiarity with asynchronous & event-driven architectures.
•
Experience with frameworks such as Spring Boot, Quarkus, Micronaut or Ktor.
•
Cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure or GCP.
•
Developing with containers
•
Understanding the difference between relational, NoSQL and other persistence technologies.
•
Experience building shared platforms, common services or greenfield technical foundations.
•
Building APIs adhering to design principles such as RESTful API design
•
Building observable systems
•
Experience in regulated or financial-services environments.
•
Exposure to payments, transaction processing or other business domains.
•
Equivalent experience with comparable technologies will be considered.
What success looks like
In this role, you will:
•
deliver valuable, production-ready features with the squad;
•
build services and APIs that are reliable, reusable and easy for others to consume;
•
improve the reliability, performance and operability of the services you work on;
•
use emerging engineering tools thoughtfully and responsibly where they add value;
•
contribute constructively to technical decisions, API standards and code reviews;
•
help the team release software safely and efficiently; and
•
support a culture of learning, collaboration and shared responsibility.

You will work as part of a cross-functional engineering squad alongside product, design and delivery colleagues. The role is expected to remain substantially hands-on, with opportunities to influence technical direction and support the development of other engineers.

This may involve occasional travel or agreed on-site working, depending on the project and client requirements.

Profit share scheme: In addition to your annual salary, you may receive a profit share defined by the company’s success in the previous year

Global and Diverse Zühlke community: witness how colleagues from all our 16 offices across the globe come together…

GLP Vendor Oversight and QA Lead
The integrity of nonclinical data depends on more than what happens inside a company's walls. Much of the critical work in GLP-regulated research — safety studies, toxicology, analytical testing — is carried out by external laboratories and CROs. When that network of partners operates to the highest quality standards, the science is sound. When it doesn't, the consequences reach all the way to patients.
This role exists to make sure it works.
Why this role matters
GLP vendor oversight is often invisible when it's done well — and very visible when it isn't. As the internal authority on GLP and nonclinical vendor quality, you will be the person others turn to when the questions are difficult. If you take data integrity seriously, understand the regulatory landscape deeply, and want to shape how a global company manages its external nonclinical network, this is a role with real scope to make a difference.
About the role
Own quality oversight of external partners supporting nonclinical and GLP activities (CROs, laboratories, test facilities). Lead the vendor lifecycle: due diligence, qualification, quality agreements, risk-based monitoring, issue management and continuous improvement, ensuring adherence to GLP/GCP/GMP, data integrity and applicable regulations. Partner with Nonclinical Development, Procurement, Legal and IT.
• Vendor Lifecycle and Governance: Run risk-based qualification and requalification, draft and maintain Quality Agreements, and set vendor KPIs and governance forums, ensuring actions and CAPAs are closed.
• Inspections: Identify and prioritise vendors for audit on a risk basis; planning, conducting and grading sits with the audit function. Confirm vendor CAPAs are fit for purpose and run effectiveness checks. Coordinate inspection readiness and front- and back-room support.
• Quality Systems and Compliance: Ensure vendor practices meet GLP/GCP/GMP, OECD GLP, 21 CFR Part 58, ICH, ISO and data integrity (ALCOA+). Provide input on third-party deviations, change control, CAPA, and the QMS.
• Risk Management and Continuous Improvement: Lead vendor risk assessments (risk registers, FMEA) to set oversight frequency, improve vendor performance, and present trends at management reviews.
• Cross-Functional Partnership: Embed quality requirements in scopes of work and contracts, guide technology transfers and data flows, and train internal stakeholders.
• Maintain and share knowledge of Regulations and Requirements: Stay current with GLP and GxP regulations and translate changes into CSL requirements.
Position Qualifications and Experience Requirements:
Education: Bachelor's degree in a relevant scientific discipline.
Experience: 3+ years of GxP quality experience with direct vendor/CRO oversight and/or auditing (GLP/GCP/GMP), nonclinical/GLP preferred. Knowledge of OECD GLP, 21 CFR Part 58, Annex 11/Part 11 and data integrity (ALCOA+). Strong communication and negotiation skills.
Competencies: Works with limited supervision across multinational teams. Strong analytical, problem-solving, influencing and organisational skills. Knowledge of QMS implementation, regulatory frameworks and audit/inspection management.
About CSL Seqirus
CSL Seqirus is part of CSL. As one of the largest influenza vaccine providers in the world, CSL Seqirus is a major contributor to the prevention of influenza globally and a transcontinental partner in pandemic preparedness. With state-of-the-art production facilities in the U.S., the U.K. and Australia, CSL Seqirus utilizes egg, cell and adjuvant technologies to offer a broad portfolio of differentiated influenza vaccines in more than 20 countries around the world.

Platform Engineer - Content Protection
About the Springer Nature Group
Springer Nature opens the doors to discovery for researchers, educators, clinicians, and other professionals. Every day, around the globe, our imprints, books, journals, platforms, and technology solutions reach millions of people. For over 175 years our brands and imprints have been a trusted source of knowledge to these communities. As AI, machine intelligence and agentic technologies reshape how research is discovered and consumed, we have a responsibility to ensure knowledge remains both discoverable and protected.
About the role
The way academic research is communicated is changing rapidly. Increasingly, Springer Nature content is being accessed through search engines, discovery platforms, AI-powered services, machine agents and content aggregation ecosystems. This creates significant opportunities to extend the reach and impact of research, but also introduces new challenges around content extraction, automated access, platform stability and commercial value protection.
The Platform Engineer - Content Protection role sits within the Off-platform Discovery and Content Protection team and is responsible for turning analytical insight and content protection strategy into operational controls. Working closely with the Data Analyst, Product Manager, Managed Security Services, SEO teams, Product teams and Platform Engineering teams, this role owns the design, implementation and operation of traffic management and content protection controls.
The role is responsible for ensuring Springer Nature can maximise discoverability while protecting content, platform performance and future business models. You will continuously evolve controls and responses to address emerging forms of automated access, including AI-driven and agentic technologies, while ensuring legitimate users retain access to our platforms and content.
Responsibilities
Content Protection Execution & Operational Ownership
• Build, operate and continuously improve WAF signals, policies and rules that detect and mitigate automated scraping, content extraction and abusive traffic.
• Own the lifecycle of traffic protection controls including design, testing, deployment, tuning, validation and retirement.
• Implement rate-limiting, bot-management and traffic-shaping strategies aligned to business objectives and platform requirements.
• Ensure protection controls are effective without negatively impacting legitimate discoverability, accessibility or customer experience.
• Turn analytical signals and intelligence into practical enforcement controls and measurable operational outcomes.
Incident Management & Response
• Lead response activities relating to scraping, automated abuse, enumeration and traffic-related incidents.
• Maintain operational playbooks and runbooks for detection, escalation, mitigation and recovery.
• Implement controls using staged rollout approaches, balancing risk reduction with customer impact.
• Monitor effectiveness of controls and continually improve protection capabilities.
Fastly Partnership & Vendor Management
• Own the day-to-day technical relationship with Fastly MSS and associated content protection tooling.
• Review, validate and operationalise Fastly recommendations and outputs.
• Work with Fastly to maximise value from platform capabilities and identify future improvement opportunities.
• Coordinate changes with stakeholders and communicate impacts, dependencies and implementation plans.
Cross-functional Collaboration & Future Capability Development
• Partner closely with the Data Analyst to operationalise detection signals and validate outcomes.
• Work with SEO teams to ensure legitimate crawlers and discovery services remain appropriately supported.
• Support Product and Platform teams with traffic-aware architectural decisions.
• Help define organisational policies relating to acceptable, non-desirable and malicious automated access.
• Contribute to future approaches for managing AI agents, machine access and emerging content consumption models.
What's Expected
In 1–3 Months:
• Build strong relationships with Managed Services vendor, Product, Platform Engineering, SEO and Analytics stakeholders.
• Develop an understanding of existing WAF configurations, controls and operating processes.
• Review recent incidents and identify immediate improvement opportunities.
• Begin establishing operational playbooks and governance processes.
By 3–6 Months you will:
• Establish repeatable workflows for traffic anomaly detection and response.
• Create clear ownership and decision-making processes for content protection activities.
• Reduce engineering involvement in reactive mitigation activities.
• Deliver measurable improvements in response capability and operational readiness.
By 6–12 Months you will:
• Operate a mature content protection capability integrated into platform operations.
• Develop trusted partnerships with Fastly and internal stakeholders.
• Improve protection against both high-volume and slow accumulation content extraction techniques.
• Lay the foundations for managing AI-driven and agentic access patterns at scale.
• Help Springer Nature balance discoverability, content protection and future commercial opportunities.
Essential Skills & Experience
• Hands-on WAF engineering experience, ideally with Fastly Next-Gen WAF (Signal Sciences) or equivalent platforms.
• Experience implementing bot management, rate limiting and traffic management controls.
• Experience responding to scraping, DDoS, automated abuse or similar traffic-management incidents.
• Strong understanding of HTTP, TLS, CDN and edge technologies.
• Ability to balance security, operational and business considerations when designing controls.
• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.
Desirable
• Experience with Fastly, Signal Sciences, edge compute or similar technologies.
• Experience working alongside security operations or managed security services teams.
• Experience with entitlement, identity or access-management systems.
• Understanding of SEO, crawler behaviour and digital discoverability ecosystems.
• Experience in academic publishing, research platforms or content-rich digital businesses.
• Experience working with emerging AI, agentic or machine-access use cases.

Alternatively, Grant Thornton
At Grant Thornton we do things differently - looking to the future, driving ambitious growth and pioneering positive change in our industry. Providing audit, tax and advisory services, we empower clients through strategic insight, curiosity, and genuine partnership. And we empower our people with real opportunity, an inclusive culture and work life balance. A true alternative.
With over 5,000 people in the UK, and a presence in 150 global markets, we're on an ambitious journey, from great to exceptional, and we need the best people to help us achieve our potential. And with that comes the opportunity to help redefine what our industry looks like, and what you want from your career.
Job Description:
MORE THAN YOU EXPECTED
Grant Thornton UK LLP is part of a global network of independent audit, tax and advisory firms, made up of some 58,000 people in over 135 countries. We're a team of independent thinkers who put quality, inclusion and integrity first. All around the world we bring a different experience to our clients. A better experience. One that delivers the expertise they need in a way that goes beyond. Personal, proactive, and agile. That's Grant Thornton.
NEW GROUND WON’T BREAK ITSELF.
Every day our teams help people in businesses and communities to do what is right and achieve their goals.
A look into the role
Our clients’ most senior decision-makers, such as CFOs, work with many parts of our firm at once. They should hear from us as one Grant Thornton, not as several separate teams. As our Buyer & Audience Programme Manager, you’ll make that happen.
Joining our Commercial Growth & Strategy team and reporting to the Head of Demand Generation, you’ll lead our firmwide programmes for a small number of priority senior buyers, starting with our Finance Leaders Programme for CFOs. This is a balanced role, roughly half strategy and half hands-on delivery. You’ll shape who we talk to, why, and what works, then brief our Campaigns team to bring it to life and guide go-to-market (GTM) leads across the firm who want to reach the same audience. It’s a new role with real room to grow: we’re starting focused, proving the model, and expanding to more buyer groups over time.
You won’t be starting from scratch. One of our largest buyer programmes is already up and running and working well, giving you a proven template to learn from and evolve, and the team has plenty of know-how to share. This is a chance to get under the skin of what our buyers really care about, put the client first, and make a real difference to how we engage them.
This is a hybrid role that can be based at any of our UK offices. We’d ask you to spend one to two days a week with your stakeholders, often in London, and a little more at the start while you build relationships.
In this role, you’ll:
• Own our priority buyer programmes, and work with the Head of Demand Generation to decide which buyer groups come next
• Set an ‘audience-first’ standard, starting from what buyers need and how they behave, and build personas that teams across the firm actually use
• Advise GTM leads and their teams on the messaging and channels that work for each buyer, including where they want a tailored version for their own sector or service line
• Convene and chair an editorial and advisory board for each buyer, bringing together service line and sector representatives to steer themes, research and content
• Own the insight behind each programme, such as a twice-yearly buyer barometer, working closely with our Head of Content
• Turn audience strategy into clear briefs for the Campaigns team, and prioritise requests within the wider campaign calendar
• Bring buyer and audience priorities into the firmwide planning cycle
• Review nurture performance across firmwide and team-led activity, spot gaps in coverage and propose how to close them
• Make sure warm interest is followed up, and help business development (BD) teams recognise when a buyer may be in market
• Build awareness among partners and directors of what the programmes offer and how to use them
Knowing you’re right for us
We’ve set ambitious growth targets for the firm, and we need the right people to help us achieve these. We’re looking for people who will bring ambition and drive to their role. In changing markets, we need to be able to work at pace and be adaptable to change and to be curious, asking questions of ourselves, each other and our clients to ensure we are delivering the services and quality we expect.
Joining us as a Manager, the minimum criteria you’ll need is experience running an audience, account-based marketing (ABM) or buyer programme across multiple business lines, and the confidence to influence senior stakeholders without formal authority.
It would be great if you had some of the following skills, but don’t worry if you don’t tick every box, we’ll help you develop along the way:
• You’ll have gained experience within professional services, financial services or another regulated environment
• You’ll have turned audience research into personas and messaging that other teams have adopted
• You’ll have written briefs that in-house or agency delivery teams can build from
• You’ll be familiar with CRM-based reporting, ideally tracking programme contribution and attribution (Microsoft Dynamics is a bonus, not essential), and how BD teams work with warm leads and in-market signals
• You’ll have strong research and analytical instincts, with the ability to spot a genuine gap in coverage or performance
• You’ll be confident presenting insight to partners and senior leaders in a way that lands as support, not instruction
• A collaborative, consultative style that makes teams want to work with you
Knowing we’re right for you
The culture at Grant Thornton is what sets us apart, we’re known for our inclusive culture and creating environments where all our people can flourish. The things that set you apart, we value them, and this helps us all to perform at our best.
Our values are the unwavering principles that shape our daily behaviours and decisions, alongside our drive to do the right thing. We’re looking for people who align with our values and are purposefully driven, actively curious and candid but kind. You can learn more about our values in practice here.
It’s not just about our culture and values, in addition to a competitive salary and reward package, you’ll also get:
-          Tailored development programmes and access to coaching
-          Flexible bank holidays – allowing you to celebrate the days that are important to you
-          Benefits including pension, life assurance and private medical, additional holiday purchasing and health benefits
-          And benefits giving you access to shopping discounts, gym memberships, financial advice
And more. Visit our benefits section to read more.
